docs.title: Compiler’s Warehouse
docs.text:
Documentation for Compiler’s analytics and business intelligence workspace.

This project provides the infrastructure and services for setting up Metabase and GCP resources.

docs.title: Project Architecture
docs.text: This section explains the reasoning behind our design choices.

docs.title: Key Architecture Decisions
docs.text: Component Selected Configuration Rationale GCP Project data-warehouse-492522 Host project containing BigQuery analytics warehouse and infrastructure. GCP Region us-west1 (Oregon) Optimal low-latency to California; standard Tier 1 GCP pricing (matches us-central1 costs). Domain & Ingress *.run.app (Cloud Run default) GCP-managed HTTPS via default Cloud Run domain; no custom domain or DNS configuration required. Container Runtime GCP Cloud Run Zero Kubernetes overhead; fully managed container lifecycle; integrated Cloud SQL proxy; native HTTPS. Instance Policy Min Instances: 1 Prevents cold-start delays and ensures Metabase background syncs, alerts, and scheduled pulses run continuously. Application Database Cloud SQL PostgreSQL Production-ready state store for Metabase (dashboards, queries, users, permissions). Never use the default embedded H2 database in production. Analytics Warehouse Google BigQuery Native driver built into Metabase. Authenticated via the Cloud Run attached Service Account (no JSON key rotation needed). Authentication Dual Auth: Google OAuth + Password Google Workspace OAuth restricted to @compiler.la for internal staff, plus password invites enabled for external stakeholders. Outbound Email Google Workspace SMTP Relay Reliable delivery of user invitations, password resets, and automated dashboard subscriptions. Secrets Management GCP Secret Manager Securely injects database passwords, encryption keys, and client secrets directly into container environment variables. Data Orchestration Google Cloud Workflows Serverless orchestration for API and file ingestion. Low-cost and scales to zero. Data Modeling dbt Core Open-source analytics modeling; run as containerized jobs on Cloud Run to avoid dedicated VMs. Ingestion Method Python Scripts Leverage existing Python libraries (e.g., Toggl access) to land raw data into GCS.

docs.title: Custom Metabase Docker Image
docs.text: This explains how the Metabase image connects to Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via Cloud Run’s built-in Cloud SQL proxy, using socat to bridge a Unix socket to TCP.

docs.title: Why a custom image?
docs.text: Metabase ships with an embedded H2 database by default. For production on Cloud Run we need it to use Cloud SQL PostgreSQL. Cloud Run mounts the Cloud SQL proxy as a Unix socket under /cloudsql/, but Metabase expects a TCP connection, so we need a bridge.

docs.title: Image layers
docs.text: metabase/Dockerfile starts from the official metabase/metabase image and adds only socat. No socket factory JAR, no classpath manipulation, no entrypoint patching.

docs.title: Entrypoint behavior
docs.text:
metabase/entrypoint.sh runs before the official Metabase entrypoint and performs these steps:

  1. Reads CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME from the environment. If unset, it auto-detects the instance name from the /cloudsql/ directory.
  2. Symlinks the Cloud SQL Unix socket into a known path inside the container.
  3. Spawns socat in the background to forward TCP port 5432 to the Unix socket.
  4. execs the official Metabase entrypoint so Metabase connects to 127.0.0.1:5432 as a normal PostgreSQL client.

If no Cloud SQL socket is present (e.g. local development via Docker Compose), the entrypoint skips all of the above and runs the official Metabase entrypoint unmodified.

docs.title: Terraform environment variables
docs.text:
Terraform injects the following environment variables into the Cloud Run service:

Variable Value Purpose CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME e.g. data-warehouse-492522:us-west1:metabase-db-40ee866c Tells the entrypoint which instance to bridge MB_DB_TYPE postgres Tells Metabase to use PostgreSQL MB_DB_HOST 127.0.0.1 Socat listens on localhost:5432 MB_DB_DBNAME metabase Database name MB_DB_USER metabase Database user MB_DB_PASS Resolved from Secret Manager Database password

Cloud Run also mounts the Cloud SQL volume at /cloudsql so the proxy socket is available at container startup. This is configured in the Terraform volume_mounts block.

docs.title: Local vs. production
docs.text: Environment Database config Behavior Cloud Run MB_DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 + CLOUD_SQL_INSTANCE_CONNECTION_NAME Socat bridges the Cloud SQL Unix socket to TCP 5432 Local (compose) MB_DB_HOST=postgres No Cloud SQL proxy — Metabase connects directly to the local PostgreSQL container. The entrypoint skips socat setup

docs.title: Upgrade path
docs.text:
When upgrading the Metabase version:

  1. Update the base image tag in metabase/Dockerfile
  2. Rebuild the image (docker compose build metabase)
  3. Test locally: docker compose up -d metabase and check logs for Successfully verified PostgreSQL
  4. Push a release tag to trigger CI/CD

docs.title: Cloud SQL Backup Verification
docs.text: This runbook covers how to verify, test, and troubleshoot automated backups for the Cloud SQL PostgreSQL instance used by Metabase.

docs.title: Backup Configuration
docs.text: Setting Value Automated backups Enabled Backup window 04:00 UTC daily Point-in-Time Recovery Enabled Transaction log retention 7 days Backup retention 15 most recent automated backups Replication log archiving Enabled

docs.title: List Recent Backups
docs.text:
gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db-'

This lists all backups for the Metabase instance, including automated and ad-hoc backups.

docs.title: Check Latest Backup
docs.text: To verify the most recent backup succeeded, check the STATE column in the output. It should show SUCCESSFUL.

docs.title: Verify Backup Retention
docs.text:
The Cloud SQL instance retains the 15 most recent automated backups. You can verify by checking the count:

gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db- AND TYPE:AUTOMATED' --format='value(NAME)' | wc -l

docs.title: Trigger an Ad-Hoc Backup
docs.text:
To create an on-demand backup (useful before major changes):

gcloud sql backups create --instance=metabase-db-<instance-suffix> --project=data-warehouse-492522

The <instance-suffix> is the random hex suffix appended to the instance name (e.g., 40ee866c). You can find it from the Terraform outputs or by listing instances:

gcloud sql instances list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='name:metabase-db-' --format='value(NAME)'

docs.title: Scheduled Backup Window
docs.text:
Automated backups start at 04:00 UTC each day. The backup window is approximately 1 hour.

  • To check when the next backup is scheduled, review the WINDOW_START_TIME from the gcloud sql backups list output.
  • Backups run outside of the backup window are ad-hoc backups.

docs.title: Restore Procedure
docs.text:
Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) is enabled with a 7-day transaction log retention window. You can restore the database to any point in the last 7 days using either a specific backup or a point-in-time timestamp.

Important: The restore procedure creates a new Cloud SQL instance (a clone). The original instance is not modified.

docs.title: Step 1: Identify the Target Backup
docs.text:
List recent backups to find the one you want to restore from:

gcloud sql backups list --project=data-warehouse-492522 --filter='instance:metabase-db-' --format='table(NAME, WINDOW_START_TIME, TYPE, STATE)'

Note the backup name and WINDOW_START_TIME.

docs.title: Step 2: Create a Clone Instance
docs.text:
Create a clone of the Metabase instance from the chosen backup:

gcloud sql instances clone metabase-db-40ee866c metabase-restore-<date> \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --point-in-time="2026-11-09T05:16:30.131Z"

Or clone from a specific backup by using the backup name as the --restorable-disk-backup flag:

gcloud sql instances clone metabase-db-40ee866c metabase-restore-<date> \
  --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --restorable-disk-backup=projects/data-warehouse-492522/backups/<backup-id>

The clone takes a few minutes to provision. Monitor progress:

gcloud sql instances describe metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522 --format='value(status)'

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the Restore
docs.text:
Connect to the clone instance and verify the data:

# Get the clone IP address
gcloud sql instances describe metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522 --format='value(ipAddresses[].ipAddress)'

# Connect via psql
psql "host=<clone-ip> dbname=metabase user=metabase"

Check key data:

-- Verify the Metabase schema version
SELECT * FROM metababase_databasefield LIMIT 10;

-- Check recent dashboard entries
SELECT dashboard_id, title, position FROM metababase_dashboard ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;

-- Verify user count matches expectations
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM metababase_user;

docs.title: Step 4: Clean Up the Clone
docs.text:
After verification, delete the clone to avoid unnecessary costs:

gcloud sql instances delete metabase-restore-<date> --project=data-warehouse-492522

docs.title: Container Image Upgrade Procedure
docs.text: This runbook covers how to upgrade the Metabase container image on Cloud Run via GitHub Actions CI/CD.

docs.title: Current Configuration
docs.text: Setting Value Service name metabase Region us-west1 Image ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase:<sha> CPU limit 1 vCPU Memory limit 4 GiB Min instances 1 Max instances 3 Container port 3000 Cloud Run URL https://metabase-2xhfhhdfxq-uw.a.run.app

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Push access to the compilerla/warehouse repository
  • Write access to the metabase/ directory (Dockerfile and entrypoint)

docs.title: 1. Update the Metabase Image
docs.text:
Edit metabase/Dockerfile to change the base image version:

FROM metabase/metabase:vX.XX.X

docs.title: 2. Push a Release Tag
docs.text:
Push a tag following the date format YYYY.MM.N to trigger the deployment:

git tag -a 2026.11.1
git push origin 2026.11.1

This triggers the Deploy GitHub Actions workflow:

  1. Build: The Dockerfile is built and pushed to GHCR (ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase:<sha>)
  2. Terraform: The new image tag is injected via TF_VAR_metabase_image_tag and applied
  3. Cloud Run: The new revision is rolled out automatically

docs.title: 3. Verify the Deployment
docs.text:
After the workflow completes, verify the deployment:

# Check the Cloud Run revision
gcloud run services describe metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --format='value(status.url)'

# Verify the running image
gcloud run services describe metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --format='value(spec.template.spec.containers[0].image)'

# Test the health endpoint
curl -f https://metabase-2xhfhhdfxq-uw.a.run.app/api/health

docs.title: Rollback Procedure
docs.text:
If a new version has issues, revert the tag and push a new one pointing to the previous version:

  1. Revert the Dockerfile to the previous Metabase version (or the previous git commit).
  2. Push a new tag to trigger a fresh deployment:
git checkout <previous-working-commit>
git tag -a 2026.11.2
git push origin 2026.11.2

docs.title: Revert to Previous Cloud Run Revision
docs.text:
If Terraform changes need to be reverted, you can also roll back to a previous Cloud Run revision:

# List revisions
gcloud run revisions list --service=metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 --region=us-west1

# Route traffic back to a previous revision
gcloud run services update-traffic metabase --project=data-warehouse-492522 \
  --region=us-west1 --to-revisions=<previous-revision-name>=100

docs.title: Database Migration Considerations
docs.text:
Metabase may include database migrations with new versions. Be aware of the following:

  • Migrations run automatically on startup when the container starts.
  • Rolling updates ensure the previous version handles requests while the new version starts.
  • If a migration fails, the previous revision can be rolled back quickly.

docs.title: Pre-Upgrade Checklist
docs.text:
• Review the Metabase release notes (https://github.com/metabase/metabase/releases) for any database migration requirements
  • Ensure the Cloud SQL backup is recent and healthy (run a backup manually if needed — see Cloud SQL Backup Verification)
  • Ensure you can rollback to the previous version

docs.title: Post-Upgrade Checklist
docs.text:
• Verify Cloud Run revision is running the new image
  • Test the /api/health endpoint returns 200 OK
  • Log in as an admin and verify dashboards load correctly
  • Check that scheduled tasks (pulses, alerts) are running

docs.title: Production Cost Estimates
docs.text: This page provides an initial monthly pricing estimate for the production environment of the Warehouse project. These figures are based on minimal production-ready configurations and low request volumes.

docs.title: Monthly Estimated Cost Breakdown
docs.text: Resource Configuration Estimated Monthly Cost Cloud SQL (PostgreSQL) 2 vCPU, 7.5 GB RAM, 10 GB SSD $60 - $90 Cloud Run (Metabase/dbt) Min instances = 1, Low volume $10 - $30 Cloud Workflows Serverless orchestration $1 - $5 BigQuery Minimal ingestion & storage $0 - $5 GCS Storage < 1 GB total $0 - $1 Total Estimated Monthly $71 - $131

docs.title: Key Assumptions & Notes
docs.text:
• Cloud SQL: Sized for a small team (approx. 20 users) to ensure smooth performance for Metabase metadata operations.
  • Cloud Run: Includes a minimum of 1 instance to eliminate “cold start” delays for users.
  • Cloud Workflows: Replaced Cloud Composer to provide a serverless, pay-per-execution model, significantly reducing the baseline infrastructure cost.
  • Data Costs: Based on current dataset sizes (~333 KB/month). Costs are expected to remain negligible until data volume scales significantly.
  • Variability: These are estimates. Actual costs may fluctuate based on specific usage patterns and GCP pricing updates in the us-west1 region.

docs.title: Deploying to Production
docs.text: This guide explains how to deploy the warehouse to production.

docs.title: Automated Deployment (Tag Push)
docs.text: Production deployments are triggered automatically by pushing a release tag to the repository. The tag pattern 2024.11.08 (date format) triggers a prod deployment.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. A release tag is pushed (e.g., git push origin 2024.11.08).
  2. GitHub Actions runs deploy.yml:
  3. Builds the custom Metabase Docker image from ./metabase/Dockerfile and pushes it to GHCR (ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase:<sha>).
  4. Terraform applies infrastructure changes, injecting the new image tag via TF_VAR_metabase_image_tag in GitHub Actions.
  5. Cloud Run rolls out the new Metabase container, which uses socat to bridge Cloud Run’s Cloud SQL Unix socket to TCP 5432 for standard PostgreSQL JDBC.
  6. If it’s a final release tag (no -rc suffix), a GitHub release is created with generated release notes.

docs.title: Required Inputs (workflow_dispatch)
docs.text:
When triggering manually via workflow_dispatch, you must provide:

  • metabase_image_tag: The Docker image tag to deploy (e.g. v0.65.2 or a Git SHA). The registry path (ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase) is hardcoded in Terraform.

docs.title: Manual Steps (Dev/Test)
docs.text: For non-production environments, the same workflow runs via workflow_dispatch with the metabase_image_tag input, or automatically via -rc release candidate tags.

docs.title: Cost Estimates
docs.text: For a detailed breakdown of the initial monthly production costs, see the Cost Estimates page.

docs.title: Infrastructure Reference
docs.text: This section contains technical details about the infrastructure.

docs.title: Cloud Run
docs.text:
• Service: metabase
  • Image: ghcr.io/compilerla/warehouse/metabase (tagged per-commit SHA, set via TF_VAR_metabase_image_tag in GitHub Actions)
  • Region: us-west1
  • Scaling: min 1, max 3 instances
  • CPU/Memory: 1 vCPU / 4 GiB RAM (limits)
  • Ingress: INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL
  • Service Account: metabase-runner@data-warehouse-492522.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  • Public Access: allUsers granted roles/run.invoker

docs.title: Cloud SQL
docs.text:
• Instance: metabase-db-{suffix} (random hex suffix, e.g. metabase-db-cba276d9)
  • Version: PostgreSQL 18
  • Tier: db-perf-optimized-N-2
  • Disk: 10 GB PD_SSD, auto-resize enabled
  • Availability: Zonal
  • Backup: enabled (point-in-time recovery, 7-day retention)
  • Database: metabase
  • User: metabase

docs.title: BigQuery
docs.text:
• Datasets (all in data-warehouse-492522, location: US):
  • raw — Data as-ingested from source systems by Airflow pipelines
  • staging — Intermediate transformation tables used between raw ingestion and analytics
  • analytics — Cleaned, transformed, and reporting-ready tables and views queried by Metabase

docs.title: GCS
docs.text:
• Bucket: compiler-data-lake
  • Location: us-west1
  • Access: uniform bucket-level access enabled

docs.title: Secret Manager
docs.text:
• metabase-db-password — PostgreSQL password for the metabase user
  • metabase-encryption-secret-key — 32-character Metabase encryption key

docs.title: IAM Service Accounts
docs.text:
• metabase-runner (metabase-runner@data-warehouse-492522.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
  • roles/bigquery.jobUser
  • roles/cloudsql.client

  • roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor

  • github-actions-runner (github-actions-runner@data-warehouse-492522.iam.gserviceaccount.com)

  • roles/editor
  • roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin
  • roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator

docs.title: Workload Identity Federation (WIF)
docs.text:
• Pool: github-actions-pool
  • Provider: github-actions-provider
  • OIDC Issuer: https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
  • Condition: assertion.repository == 'compilerla/warehouse'
  • Binding: github-actions-runner service account granted roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser via the WIF pool

docs.title: Enabled APIs
docs.text:
• bigquery.googleapis.com
  • cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com
  • iam.googleapis.com
  • run.googleapis.com
  • secretmanager.googleapis.com
  • sqladmin.googleapis.com
  • sql-component.googleapis.com
  • vpcaccess.googleapis.com

docs.text:
The following helper scripts are available to run inside the dev container:

docs.title: Getting Started with Compiler’s Warehouse
docs.text: This is a tutorial on how to set up your local development environment.

docs.title: Local Development (VS Code Dev Containers)
docs.text:
This repository follows Compiler’s cross-platform Dev Containers standard to ensure consistent development environments across macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Note

Read our blog post on Dev Containers to learn more about Compiler’s cross-platform development philosophy.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Docker and Docker Compose running locally (check out Podman for a cross-platform OSS management environment).
  2. Visual Studio Code.
  3. VS Code Dev Containers Extension.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Create and configure your local environment file:
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env to set your desired values. The metabase service will connect to the local postgres service using the MB_DB_TYPE/MB_DB_HOST/MB_DB_DBNAME values from this file.

  1. Open this folder in VS Code.
  2. When prompted, click “Reopen in Container” (or press F1 / Ctrl+Shift+P / Cmd+Shift+P and run Dev Containers: Reopen in Container).
  3. VS Code will build the dev container and launch all three services:
  4. dev: Your development shell containing terraform, gcloud, pre-commit, and Postgres client tools.
  5. postgres: Local PostgreSQL 18 database storing Metabase application state.
  6. metabase: Custom Metabase application (socat bridges Cloud SQL Unix socket to TCP 5432 for prod; connects directly to local postgres for dev) connecting to local postgres. Available at http://localhost:3000.
